brand-orange.notes: User-pinned SheepIt identity colour. Dark theme accent. Permitted in exactly three places: actionable elements, the current selection, and the single element that stands for the viewer (the one accent-washed tag per machine or render-key row included).

accent-deep.notes: Light theme accent. Same hue driven down in lightness: white on the pinned brand orange is 3.2:1, white on this is 5.3:1.

accent-weak.notes: The accent as a fill behind something, never as a colour on something. Dark value shown; the light-theme twin is rgba(182,71,47,.10). Used by pressed segments, chips, the current-user table row, the machine tag, the in-use key badge, and ::selection.

field-ink.notes: Label colour that sits on brand orange in the dark theme. The brand hex may not move, so the label does. Also the switch knob's fill when the switch is on, through the --btn-ink token.

ink-on-accent.notes: Light theme label on the deepened accent (5.3:1). Also the switch knob in the light theme.

canvas.notes: Dark page field. Not pure black, so raised surfaces have room in both directions.

canvas-light.notes: Light page field. Not pure white, so white panels remain distinguishable from it.

surface.notes: Default container surface in the dark theme: panels, tables, the metric band, buttons, the mode button and the mode pill.

surface-light.notes: Default container surface in the light theme.

surface-raised.notes: Hover and inset fill: table row hover, nav hover, avatar initial fallback, skeleton shimmer midpoint, the list avatar well.

surface-raised-light.notes: Light-theme twin of the raised tier.

surface-sunken.notes: Recessed fill: empty heatmap cells, the progress-bar track, tooltip and toast backgrounds, the switch track at rest, the idle key badge.

surface-sunken-light.notes: Light-theme twin of the sunken tier.

hairline.notes: Every border in the system, including the internal dividers of a multi-cell band, the table's row rules, and the account list's frame and row rules (same colour both places). Always 1px, always solid.

hairline-strong.notes: The border one step up, for what must read as interactive: icon buttons, the mode button, inputs, the switch track on hover, scrollbar thumbs, tooltip outlines, the chart crosshair, the hovered heatmap cell.

ink.notes: Headings, metric values, and the dark-theme body copy that carries meaning. Also the mode pill's label, hard-coded because no token reaches it.

ink-secondary.notes: Supporting prose, table cell text, nav labels, inline metadata, the mode button's label, a machine's specification. Also the default label of every ghost button.

ink-tertiary.notes: The quiet layer: axis labels, column headers, KPI captions, units, hints, footers, the switch knob at rest, the key comment, the machine row's exit link. Deliberately still readable — small-and-faint is not the same as restrained.

positive.notes: The only semantic colour. One derived delta inside one KPI caption. No red, no amber, no warning ramp — errors are stated in words, and a failed write is reported by the toast, not by the button.

positive-light.notes: Light-theme positive, deepened for the same contrast reason as the accent.

display.purpose: The account name in the identity strip. The largest non-numeric text in the product.

headline.purpose: Empty-state title and the monthly best/worst values. Statements, not labels.

title.purpose: Panel headers, section headers, the top-bar product mark, the error-state headline, every account panel including the second heading inside the blacklist panel. Panels are titled rather than headed.

metric.purpose: The four KPI values. The only place the ramp is allowed to be loud, and the only text permitted negative tracking as display treatment.

metric-narrow.purpose: The KPI values below the 560px breakpoint, where four 27px figures would truncate.

metric-band.purpose: The four farm-status values. Smaller than the KPI tier because they are secondary readings.

body.purpose: The 14px root size and the table's baseline. Row names take 550 when they need to lead their row.

label.purpose: Navigation, segment buttons, table status text, identity metadata, hints, captions, the switch label and its hint line.

micro-label.purpose: KPI captions, column headers, legend text, the heatmap note. One step below it sits the 11px floor: axis ticks, the heat map's weekday column and month labels, the month-bar labels, the PLUS badge, the CPU/GPU chips, the numbered step marker, the render key's in-use badge, the tooltip's date line. Nothing is set below 11px, and nothing at 11px carries a sentence.

shadows.name: ambient-panel-dark
shadows.purpose: The default and only elevation in the dark theme: metric band, panels, the farm band, tooltips, toasts, the mode pill. A tight contact shadow plus a wide soft one, so a panel reads as sitting a millimetre above the field rather than as a drop shadow. Also carried by the --shadow token on #sp, and hard-coded by the mode pill because in its mode the token does not exist.

shadows.name: ambient-panel-light
shadows.purpose: The same construction at the strength a light field can absorb, tuned toward the neutral ink hue so the shadow stays cool rather than sooty.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Every hover, focus and pressed change. Short enough that a mouse crossing a table does not produce a light show.

motion.name: switch-throw
motion.purpose: The switch: the track's fill and border swap while the knob travels exactly its own width (14px) inside the 34×20 track. The only motion in the account surface, and it is a state change, not an entrance.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The system's only authored curve. Carries the one-time entrance rise and the points curve's draw-on.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: One-time entrance for the metric band (0s), the 8/4 working area (.06s), and the farm band (.1s) — a staggered 4px rise, fired once per view render.

motion.name: area-rise
motion.purpose: The chart's area fill fades and rises once, slightly behind the line.

motion.name: curve-draw
motion.purpose: The points curve draws itself once on first paint, driven by getTotalLength() so the timing is exact rather than guessed.

motion.name: tooltip-fade
motion.purpose: Chart and heatmap tooltip appearing and leaving under the pointer. Position is set imperatively, never transitioned.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: The 26px loading ring: 2px hairline track with a single accent arc.

motion.name: skeleton-shimmer
motion.purpose: 400%-wide tonal sweep between the surface and raised tiers for skeleton rows.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Gates the entrance animations and the curve draw entirely; hover and focus still change colour, because a colour change is not motion.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The 8/4 working area collapses to a single column, and the top bar's mode button drops its label to keep the icon.

breakpoints.name: medium
breakpoints.purpose: Metric band and farm band fold to 2x2 with internal rules reassigned; the top bar's timestamp surrenders first.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Page gutters drop 24px to 16px; tables keep their columns at a 660px min-width and scroll; the heatmap switches from aspect-ratio cells to fixed 14px cells with horizontal scroll, its month labels to fixed 14px columns, and its weekday column is dropped entirely; the empty state's three steps stack.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Top bar tightens; the username surrenders because the identity strip already carries the name; the brand's PLUS badge drops and the nav labels shorten to 排行/账户 rather than scrolling or hiding.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: KPI cells and farm cells drop to 15px/14px padding and their values to 22px/16px; month bars shorten to 96px; machine rows wrap rather than truncate their specification; the empty-state inner block eases to 32px/18px.

surfaces.name: page-column
surfaces.purpose: The single centred column every view is built in.

surfaces.name: form-column
surfaces.purpose: Forms run narrower than the page column on purpose: a form is read one control per line, and a full-width input row is a longer reach than a target needs to be.

surfaces.name: top-bar
surfaces.value: min-height: 56px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 86%, transparent); backdrop-filter: saturate(1.6) blur(12px)
surfaces.purpose: Sticky, with a 1px hairline under it. The only backdrop filter in the shell; falls back to the solid page field where color-mix is unsupported. Order left to right: brand, nav, spacer, timestamp, mode button, refresh, identity.

surfaces.name: mode-pill
surfaces.value: position: fixed; left: 14px; bottom: 14px; z-index: 2147482000; opacity: .62 (1 on hover)
surfaces.purpose: The only element that renders while the main stylesheet is deliberately not loaded, so it hard-codes the dark surface, primary ink, a white-alpha hairline and the dark ambient shadow instead of reading a token. It stays dark in the light theme and sits below the shell's z-index, so it can never float over the interface it came from.

surfaces.name: stack-gap
surfaces.purpose: The vertical gap between every region on the page.

surfaces.name: log-scrollport
surfaces.value: max-height: min(58vh, 560px); overflow: auto; thead th { position: sticky; top: 0 } — opened from a secondary button that states the event count
surfaces.purpose: The session page’s activity summary (default) and its full log (behind one button). 761 raw events printed as a table made the page 4988px tall with the diagnostics unreachable and every row mostly whitespace; the summary answers "was this machine working" in five rows, and the raw log keeps its own scrollport and stuck header for when the detail is actually wanted.

contrastNotes: White on #e06d58 is 3.2:1 and fails the 4.5:1 floor, so the dark theme pairs the pinned brand orange with the near-black #0f1218 (5.7:1).
White on the deepened light accent #b6472f is 5.3:1.
The brand hex is a hard constraint; the label is the variable. The switch knob is the same label: it takes --btn-ink when the track is on, so the contrast decision is inherited rather than re-made.

components.name: Data Table
components.description: Hairline-ruled rows, no vertical rules, no zebra striping; hover moves the whole row to the raised tier. The current user's row takes the ember wash and appends a small "you" marker — the accent's third permitted job. The publisher cell may carry one maintenance action and only one: a labelled secondary toggle whose text is the state — Prioritise when the publisher is outside your render-priority list, Remove when they are inside it — so the reader never holds a list in their head to know what the click does. It stays out of the way until the row is engaged: on a pointer device the button is transparent until the row is hovered or focus lands inside it, hidden by opacity rather than display so it never leaves the tab order, and on a touch device it is simply always visible. Membership itself is never hover-dependent — a publisher already in your list carries a persistent 12px accent star after their name. The action is absent for your own rows and absent entirely when the list could not be read. The publisher's name in a project row and the user's name in a ranking row are links to that person's profile; the accent appears only on hover, because colouring a whole column of names turns the table into a wall of links. Beside the labelled toggle sits a 3-dot button opening a small menu of the two list actions that are not toggles — donate your points to this publisher, blacklist them — each item carrying a check and flipping its wording when the publisher is already on that list. The menu is positioned by measurement with its left edge aligned to the trigger, so it unfolds to the right of the button rather than hanging back across the row; near the bottom of the viewport it flips upward, and near the right edge it slides left instead of overflowing. It is never an absolutely positioned child of the table: the table's own scroll container would clip it on the bottom rows.

components.name: Row Action Menu
components.description: The 3-dot button in a publisher cell and the small menu it opens, holding the two list actions that are not toggles: donate the points you earn to this publisher, or blacklist them so their projects are never sent to you. Each item leads with an icon for what the action is (a heart for donating, a prohibition sign for blacklisting), and the check that marks "already on this list" sits at the trailing edge rather than sharing the leading slot, so the two meanings never crowd one another. A checked item also flips its wording into the undo. The button follows the table's row-action rule (hidden by opacity until the row is hovered or focused) but stays visible while its own menu is open, tracked by aria-expanded. The menu is positioned by measurement and aligned to the table's right edge, not to the trigger: the publisher column sits on the left, so a menu hung off the button would cover the very name just clicked, and the table's scroll container would clip an absolutely positioned child on the bottom rows.

components.description: The session page’s default reading of 761 events: one row per day (per month once the session is older than a month), newest first, capped at fourteen rows with a tertiary line naming what is left out (days or months, whichever the buckets are). Four numbers per row — render time, events, jobs, send failures — plus a 6px accent bar at 55% drawn from the rendering time. The bar keeps one meaning: a machine that has never rendered anything gets unfilled tracks, never a bar quietly counting events under a column still labelled render time; the gutter holding it is never removed, because that flex column is what keeps the header labels over their own numbers. Keys carry a year once the record crosses one, and the failures column exists only when there are failures. The bar is scaled to the busiest period in the same record — the largest bucket is always full — so it reads as a shape rather than an absolute measurement, and the four numbers beside it carry the values; the scale covers the whole record, not just the fourteen rows shown.

narrative.overview:
This is a read-out, not a landing page. Every view exists so that a contributor can glance at it and be told the truth about their own labour: how much they have rendered, how the curve is bending, and where they sit among five hundred other people. The world that carries that job is deliberately the category-standard one — a neutral grey field, hairline rules, tabular numerals, one accent — executed without a single shortcut. Familiarity is the point: the structure should be invisible so the numbers are not.

The system has two temperatures and only one voice. Surfaces step through three neutral tiers by tint alone; separation comes from a 1px border, never from a line of colour or a glow. Type runs down a single sans stack in seven narrow steps, and anything that could be read as a quantity is tabular-aligned so columns of digits stay in vertical register. Into that grey field goes one warm colour, and it is spent with intent: brand orange marks what you can act on, what is currently selected, and the one series that represents you. Everything else — statuses, project names, machine counts, the entire ranking table — stays neutral, including the things that feel like they deserve a badge. The account page is the first surface that changes something rather than showing something, and it holds the same line: one accent-filled commit per panel, and every maintenance action behind it a quiet bordered button.

Depth is nearly flat. There are exactly two shadows in the system and both are ambient rather than structural: a two-part soft shadow that keeps a panel off the page by a millimetre, and a darker twin for the dark theme. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing is glass. Where the older interface it replaces failed, it failed by compression — labels truncated, progress numbers printed across a two-tone bar, six columns crushed into 620px while half the viewport sat empty. This system answers every one of those failures the same way: give the content the space it needs and let it be read.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral grey tonal field, three surface tiers, 1px hairlines as the only separator.
One warm accent with three permitted jobs; everything else is neutral by default, not by omission.
Tabular numerals everywhere a number can appear.
Near-flat depth: two ambient shadows, plus tone and border for layering.
Data-density by subject: compact rows in tables and lists, breathing room around charts.
Chinese-first type with the English base language as an equal-weight fallback, both on the system UI stack.
A visible exit: the shell is a mode, the way out is a button in its own top bar, and the way back is a pill that renders while the rest of the system is switched off.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Brand orange is spent on exactly three jobs: actionable elements, the current selection, and the one series or element in data that represents "you". A fourth use is a defect. Status text stays neutral on purpose — painting "Rendering" orange turns the table into a wall of orange and dilutes what the colour means everywhere else.

rules.name: The Two Sets Rule
rules.body: The light theme is not the dark theme inverted. Surfaces get brighter, borders get fainter, and the accent deepens until white text clears the contrast floor on it. Every token has a light twin and both are normative.

rules.name: The No Decorative Colour Rule
rules.body: Hue never enters as decoration. There are no gradients used as ornament, no glass, no coloured status pills, no icon medallions. The only gradient in the product is the fade under the points curve, and it fades the accent to nothing.

rules.name: The Tabular Truth Rule
rules.body: Any string that could be read as a quantity carries tabular numerals — KPI values, table figures, axis ticks, the heatmap total and peak, the progress numerator, the "showing n / total" counters, the month labels, and the render keys, which are strings that still have to line up like numbers. This is applied through one utility class rather than repeated declarations, so a number that is not aligned is a missing class, not a judgement call.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: One font stack for everything, including numerals and code-like strings. A second face has to earn its place, and nothing in this product needs one.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: One shadow token, two themes, one role. Shadows mark "this is a container"; they never mark hover, focus, selection, or importance. If an element needs to look more important, change its tone or its position, not its blur radius.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A border is the separator. Cards are not nested inside cards, and a divider inside a group is the same colour as the border around it — never lighter, never dashed.

rules.name: The No Medallion Rule
rules.body: No icon is ever placed inside a coloured shape to give it weight. Icons are 14–15px of `currentColor` sitting next to their label at the same optical weight — the top bar's refresh control is a 30px boxed icon button, and that border is a hit target, not a decoration.

rules.name: The One Commit Rule
rules.body: A panel ends in exactly one accent-filled primary button — the action that changes something on the server. Every other action in that panel, delete included, is a secondary button on the surface fill and the hairline border; there is no third button tier, and there is still no red one. A maintenance action is not painted, it is worded.

rules.name: The Unknown Field Rule
rules.body: A parsed field with no entry in the vocabulary is printed with its raw label instead of being dropped. Silence about a field the site chose to show is a data loss, not tidiness — and the site does add fields.

rules.name: The Summarise Before Printing Rule
rules.body: A record is summarised by its own natural period before it is printed — a day is the unit a person asks about a machine, so a day is the row — and the raw rows go behind one button that says how many there are. When they are opened they get their own scrollport with a stuck header; a log is allowed to be long, the page it sits on is not.

rules.name: The Relative Bar Rule
rules.body: The activity bar is scaled to the busiest period in the same record: the largest bucket is always full and every other bucket is a fraction of it. That makes the bar a shape and not a measurement — it answers "how did this day compare with this machine's own best day" and cannot answer "how busy is this machine against another", because two records with different maxima both end in a full-length bar. An absolute scale would flatten every ordinary day against one outlier, and the four numbers beside the bar carry the values. The scale is taken over the whole record rather than the fourteen rows on screen, so folding the tail away leaves the visible bars where they were; and a period that rendered at all is never invisible, because the fill floors at 3px and a half-percent day would otherwise round to nothing.

rules.name: The One Clock Rule
rules.body: Every timestamp the system renders is the reader’s local time, and the surface says so once instead of leaving two clocks on one screen. The site’s own raw strings stay inside the facts grid, under a header that already says the values are unconverted; a derived figure that can be expressed on the reader’s clock is expressed there — the "since" line comes from the first logged event, not from the server’s creation string, because those two differ by the server’s offset and reading them side by side looks like six lost hours.

rules.name: The Borrowed Controls Rule
rules.body: On a partly-rebuilt page the working controls are moved, not rebuilt. The site's upload form carries its submit in an onsubmit attribute bound to its own script, its estimator carries a jQuery autocomplete bound by an inline script, and its progress bar is fed by the site's own poller — all addressed by id and handler attributes rather than by appearance, so relocating the nodes into our card keeps every handler alive (measured after the move: the form's onsubmit still resolves, the autocomplete still holds its ui-autocomplete data, and the estimator's endpoint still answers). Re-drawing that markup means reimplementing upload, progress polling and device lookup on our side — and reimplementing them again every time the site touches them. Move the nodes, then strip the site's look with a scoped reset and put ours on.

rules.name: The Destructive-Replacement Rule
rules.body: A block-level translation is `el.innerHTML = <translation>`, so it is never applied to a container holding anything that works. Measured before the fix: the site puts "Max: 2,048 MB before ZIP compression…" and the `<input type="file">` in the same `<td>`, and the block entry for that sentence deleted the file picker — leaving every reader with translation on holding an upload form that could not be submitted, which is to say exactly the readers the feature exists for. Enforced in the translator, not the dictionary: a candidate containing an input, select, textarea, button, label, form, svg, canvas, video or iframe is left alone. Links stay fair game, because a block translation exists for sentences cut apart by `<a>` and `<strong>` and its value carries them. When a sentence cannot be translated safely, say it ourselves from a fact we read — the size note in the upload card is our wording carrying the site's own number.

dos: Do keep brand orange to its three jobs, and audit for the fourth: a rendered run of the projects table should show orange only on the progress fills, the selected CPU/GPU markers, the "you" marker, and the primary button.
Do use one bordered surface with internal hairlines for any band of peer metrics (the KPI band, the farm band); reassign which internal edge is drawn when the band folds to 2×2.
Do put `tabular-nums` on every quantity, including axis ticks, legend totals, month labels, render keys, and the "showing n / total" counters.

Do size data visualisations so a single unit is readable — 53 weeks at ~20px per cell full-bleed, 14px plus horizontal scroll on narrow screens — and prefer moving a visualisation to full width over shrinking it into a side column.
Do move a label out of a bar, out of a truncated `<dl>`, or onto its own line rather than shrinking its type or letting it be cut off; the previous interface's defects were all compression defects.
Do state failures in words with a retry action, and degrade a failed parse to a local "no data" instead of an empty-state story or a thrown error.

Do theme the browser surfaces from the palette — selection wash, accent caret, thin scrollbar on the strong hairline, and a 2px accent focus ring at a 2px offset — and keep `text-underline-offset` at 3px with a 1px thickness on links.
Do keep hover a colour change and reserve motion for the one-time entrance: a 500–700ms rise from 4px with `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`, and state transitions at 100–120ms.

Do keep the way out of a mode visible from inside it, and let the pill that brings the user back carry its own styles: it renders while the stylesheet is deliberately not loaded, so it reads no tokens and is allowed to read none. Word it as the action rather than the state, and make it opaque — a subdued chip is not "quiet", it is missing.

Do hide a control visually instead of removing it: `display: none` deletes it from the tab order, so a 1px transparent input that still takes focus — with the ring drawn on the label through `:focus-within` — is the pattern for anything a platform will not let you style.
Do summarise a long record by its natural period before printing it, and put the raw rows behind one button that states how many there are.
Do print a field the vocabulary does not recognise, with its raw label, and keep a secret revealed only by the click that asks for it.
Do join a fact the page does not carry back on from the page that does — the publisher of a renderable project — and leave it blank when the join cannot resolve, rather than guessing.
Do say once, on the surface, which clock its timestamps are on — and keep the site’s own raw time strings inside the panel that is explicitly unconverted.

Do keep a row-level action out of the way until the row is engaged (opacity behind :hover and :focus-within, never display:none, always visible where there is no hover), state membership with a persistent mark, and make the toggle say its own state in the label — dropping it entirely when the membership is unknown.

Do move a working control instead of re-implementing it, and treat the site's ids and handler attributes as the contract: bindings are addressed by id, not by appearance, so relocating a node keeps its handler and re-drawing it throws the handler away.
Do give a half-rebuilt region its own background and its own surface, and assume the surrounding page's theme is not the reader's — measured, the site in light while our tokens resolved dark.

Do state, on a surface whose numbers come from the site's configuration, that they were read at that moment rather than written into the script — and read them, since the site's own repository defaults are not what it is serving (live: 12,000 tiles and 4096x2160 against defaults of 3,000 and 3840x2160).
Do leave an exit on a full-page takeover: when the guard hides the site's own navigation, the shell and the switch back to the classic interface are the way out, not decoration.
donts: Don't colour status text or add semantic pills. "Rendering", "Waiting" and "Paused" stay neutral secondary ink — a wall of orange statuses destroys the accent's meaning and its usefulness. One named exception, decided 2026-10-04: the session page's single machine-state chip, because a machine you are paying for is either working or not and that is the one status a reader must not have to hunt for. It spends no new hue — running is the accent filled with the near-black ink, paused is the accent at its 14% wash with accent ink — so the two read as loud and quiet on one colour rather than as two meanings of two colours. It stays one chip per page: this is a machine-state chip, not a licence to colour table statuses.
Don't split a peer-metric band into four cards, and never nest a card inside a card.

Don't use decorative gradients, glassmorphism, blurred backdrops, coloured icon medallions, or hover lift. The one gradient in the product is the accent fading to transparent under the points curve, and the one backdrop filter is the shell's sticky top bar, filled with the page field mixed to 86% and blurred.
Don't paint a maintenance action or hide it behind an icon. Remove and delete are secondary buttons that word what they remove; the accent belongs to the commit, and there is still no red.

Don't reach for a smaller, fainter grey as a substitute for restraint. The muted ink is readable at 11px, which is the floor, and 11px is spent on axis ticks and badges — never on a sentence. Small-and-faint is not the same thing as disciplined.
Don't use white text on the pinned brand orange, or lighten the brand orange to make white work — move the label to the near-black ink instead. The brand hex is a hard constraint; the label is not.
Don't reflow tables into stacked cards on narrow screens. Keep the columns, let the table scroll, and keep "show more" stating how many of how many.
Don't add a second typeface, a webfont, a second accent hue, or a red. One face, one voice, and errors said in words.
Don’t repeat a grouped reason on every row. When thirty rows carry six sentences, the reason is the grouping — print it once, above the names it explains.
Don’t print a raw record as a page’s default reading, and don’t print a render key on load. Both make the record louder than the machine it describes.
Don’t colour-code event types or invent a status ramp to make a log look informative. The accent bar carries one measure; everything else is text.
Don’t let a chart quietly change what it measures. If the only measure that exists is not the one the column is named after, drop the chart instead of relabelling it in silence.
Don’t make a control hover-only. A mouse-only affordance is unreachable by keyboard and invisible on touch; reveal it only where hovering exists, and keep whatever it tells you visible without it.

Don’t re-draw a control that already works just because you are rebuilding the surface it sits on — and read from the other side, don’t let a block-level translation run on a container holding anything functional, because it is an innerHTML assignment and it deleted the file picker once.
Don’t drop a partly-rebuilt region onto a host page without its own surface and background: nothing around it was built to hold it, and the host page’s theme is the site’s, not the reader’s.
